designDirection: Third concept: single connected anvil-bow flagship, stepped hull, offset command citadel. User rejected the trident and plain wedge.

prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: five-view 2D spaceship reference sheet for a NEW TITAN flagship design.

The user has rejected TWO earlier Titan directions: a three-pronged / three-headed trident, and a plain triangular wedge. Create a striking THIRD concept with a different silhouette. It must be a single connected spacecraft, neither a wedge nor a cluster of forward arms.

DESIGN: a colossal armored fleet carrier / flagship, with a broad TRANSVERSE HAMMERHEAD BOW, a deep continuous central hull, stepped angular shoulders, and a massive rectangular stern drive block. The hammerhead is ONE continuous armored structure across the nose, smoothly and structurally joined to the central hull by a wide solid neck, not two separate forward pods. Overall proportions about 1.8 times as long as maximum beam. The forward transverse bow is clipped and chamfered like a heavy industrial anvil, with a shallow concave central face and several inset sensor windows. It must not be pointed, triangular, split, or forked. The midsection has a strong stepped outline: broad front crossbar, narrower but substantial central body, then broad aft shoulder armor. No thin connector stalks.
Give it a memorable slightly asymmetric command arrangement: a compact terraced command citadel on the STARBOARD AFT shoulder (viewer right in TOP), balanced by a long dark inset flight-deck/service trench on the PORT AFT shoulder (viewer left in TOP). This is surface asymmetry within a coherent mostly balanced silhouette, not extra ship heads. A large octagonal armored reactor/service cover sits on the aft centerline. Two deep recessed hangar entrances sit in the lateral mid-hull sidewalls, integrated INTO the body. Four substantial twin-barrel dorsal gun turrets, two on each side of the central hull, all aimed forward. Small point-defense emplacements and antennas provide scale. Distinctive layered slab armor, bold dark structural recesses, docking apertures, radiator blocks, exposed machinery only within protected inset pockets. The design should feel like an intimidating mobile fortress with a strong identity and believable connected construction.

NO trident, NO three noses, NO long forward outriggers, NO separated hull branches, NO triangular wedge, NO pointed spear bow, NO thin fuselage with oversized wings, NO circular flying saucer, NO cargo containers, NO giant fighter cockpit. Do not imitate a named franchise spacecraft.

Six main stern drives in TWO groups of THREE, side by side horizontally, separated by a substantial central armored reactor keel. All six nozzles are on one horizontal centerline and face directly rearward. Their cylindrical housings stay integrated into the stern block. Cyan cores with dark layered metal rims; no long exhaust.

MATERIALS: same Stellar Syndicates ship family: pale titanium and off-white armor, dark charcoal gunmetal structure, restrained brass edge trim and fasteners, small cyan light strips and bridge windows. Fine surface wear and panel seams; broad strong shapes first, detailed machinery second. Precise, fully colored hard-surface technical concept illustration with crisp dark contours and gentle neutral shading.

SHEET: exactly FIVE consistent complete drawings on a wide landscape canvas, approximately 2:1 aspect ratio, clean warm-white background. Large TOP and BOTTOM on the left, both nose UP, equal length and beam. FRONT upper right, BACK middle right, SIDE lower right with nose LEFT. Comfortable margins, no overlap or cropping. Clear title "TITAN" and labels "TOP", "BOTTOM", "FRONT", "BACK", "SIDE" only. No extra text, dimensions, hero render, comparison ships, starfield, grid overlays, logos or watermark.

ORTHOGRAPHIC PROJECTIONS:
TOP: directly overhead. Show the bold anvil-like transverse bow, stepped connected hull, offset starboard aft bridge, port service trench, centerline octagonal reactor cover, four dorsal turrets, and six stern drive housings. Preserve big readable shapes.
BOTTOM: true underside view, nose UP, same physical hull dimensions and profile. Interpret the viewing direction correctly: asymmetric starboard and port details reverse left/right when observed from below. Entire underside fully textured with ventral armor terraces, a recessed central keel, radiator banks, maintenance and docking hatches, cyan service lights, and protected machinery. No copied dorsal command citadel, no dorsal turrets stamped onto the belly, no plain blank gray surface, no landing legs. Same six engines.
FRONT: exact level head-on orthographic, zero elevation. The broad hammerhead presents its ONE connected face across the bow, with a low armored central recess, not a pointed nose. Fore-aft length collapses. Compact offset command citadel rises modestly behind the bow on the physically correct side. Visible forward guns show small muzzle ends, not sideways-projecting barrels. No visible rear exhausts through the hull.
BACK: exact level stern-on orthographic, matching the front's scale. Show six round cyan apertures as three on either side of the central armored keel, in ONE horizontal row. Command citadel appears on the opposite page side from FRONT because the observer faces the other direction. Show solid backs of forward-facing gun mounts, not backward-facing muzzle holes.
SIDE: a genuine level starboard-side elevation, nose LEFT and stern RIGHT. Show the transverse bow as a solid thick bow section joined to the full-depth hull, stepped shoulders, the aft command citadel, inset hangar sidewall, layered belly and engine housings pointing RIGHT. Matching positions and proportions across all views. No overhead or three-quarter view.

Prioritize an ORIGINAL, memorable, powerful silhouette and consistency between all five projections.
